macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin briefly tops $79,000 before easing as ETF flows and CLARITY Act optimism lift sentiment
items.summary: Bitcoin surged above $79,286 in early trading before slipping back to around $77,282, with the move driven by institutional demand, ETF inflows, and renewed optimism around the CLARITY Act. The asset was still up 0.31% over 24 hours and 22.07% for the week, according to the report.

items.title: Bitcoin nears US$80,000 amid biggest weekly rally in three years
items.summary: Bitcoin jumped as much as 9.4% and traded around US$77,500 in late New York trading, marking its strongest weekly rally in three years. The move reflects broad bullish momentum across the crypto market.

items.title: Bitcoin slips under $77,000 as traders reassess rally and miner economics
items.summary: Bitcoin fell to about $76,536 after giving up earlier gains that had pushed it to $77,468, as investors weighed improving miner profitability and arguments that the bear market may be maturing. The report said the coin was down 0.8% over 24 hours.

items.title: Crypto market turns volatile with sharp weekend selloff and heavy liquidations
items.summary: Chinese-language market coverage reported Bitcoin down more than 2%, Ethereum down 5.29%, and several major altcoins falling sharply, including ADA, XRP, and XLM. CoinGlass data cited in the report showed 179,200 contracts liquidated in 24 hours, totaling about $882 million.

items.title: EU sanctions package expands restrictions on banks and cryptocurrency networks
items.summary: The European Union adopted its 21st sanctions package against Russia, expanding restrictions that include banks, cryptocurrency networks, and oil trade. The measure adds another regulatory and compliance pressure point for crypto-related flows tied to sanctioned entities.

items.title: India’s central bank reiterates preference for crypto policy leaning toward prohibition
items.summary: Reuters-reported internal government documents say India’s central bank continues to favor a policy 'leaning towards prohibition,' warning that crypto assets and stablecoins could threaten financial stability and monetary sovereignty. The stance signals continued regulatory caution in one of the world’s largest crypto markets.

items.title: Bitcoin, Ethereum and major altcoins trade mixed after broader market pause
items.summary: A market snapshot showed Bitcoin up 0.11% at $77,357.55 and Ethereum up 0.97% at $2,450, while XRP, Solana, and Dogecoin were lower. The same report highlighted strong gains in smaller tokens such as Morpho, Cash Cat, and Pudgy Penguins.

items.title: Solana governance vote and Tether mining exit highlighted among notable project developments
items.summary: A crypto news roundup pointed to a Solana governance vote that could double the network’s deflation rate and Tether ending Bitcoin mining operations in Uruguay. It also flagged stablecoin-industry efforts to expand identification rules.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Z.ai launches GLM-5.3 model
items.summary: Chinese AI firm Z.ai has launched its new GLM-5.3 model, adding another major release to the rapidly moving open-model market. The available reporting does not include detailed benchmark data or pricing in the search results.

items.title: Google unveils Gemini 3.7 Flash for coding and agent workflows
items.summary: Google has introduced Gemini 3.7 Flash, positioning it for coding and agentic workflow use cases. Separate reporting indicates Google also cut pricing for the model to roughly half of the previous version.

items.title: Alibaba Cloud launches Wan 3.0 video generation model
items.summary: Alibaba Cloud's Wan 3.0 video generation model has officially gone live and can generate up to 30 seconds of video per prompt. This signals continued competition in multimodal generative AI, especially in China.

items.title: Nvidia said to unveil financing initiative for AI chip purchases
items.summary: Nvidia has reportedly unveiled a major financing initiative to help support purchases of artificial intelligence chips. If confirmed, the move would highlight how AI infrastructure demand is increasingly being supported through vendor financing and broader capital-market mechanisms.

items.title: OpenAI lowers developer pricing for GPT-5.6 Sol
items.summary: OpenAI reportedly cut benchmark pricing for its front-line GPT-5.6 Sol model by more than 20%, with the discounted rate offered for three months. The pricing move reflects intensifying competition among frontier model providers.

items.title: AI model price competition intensifies
items.summary: Reporting across the day describes a broader price war in foundation models, with OpenAI and Google both lowering prices. The trend suggests that cheaper inference and aggressive pricing are becoming a key competitive lever.

items.title: OpenAI warns about advanced AI cyberattacks and pauses some frontier training
items.summary: OpenAI's global affairs chief warned that frontier models are beginning to enable planning and execution of complex cyberattacks, and said the company has paused some frontier training to improve safety protections. The warning adds to growing concern about dual-use capabilities in advanced AI.

items.title: Anthropic models leaked in third-party app listings
items.summary: Reporting says two new Anthropic model names, 'claude-mashmallow-eap' and 'claude-melon-eap,' were exposed through third-party developer applications and community discovery. The apparent leak points to active product development ahead of formal announcement.

items.title: xAI expands Grok Build to all plans
items.summary: xAI has made Grok Build available across web, iOS, Android, and all subscription tiers, allowing users to create apps, games, websites, and dashboards from natural language. The rollout broadens access to xAI's consumer app-building tools.

items.title: Nvidia AVO reportedly achieves perfect ARC-AGI-3 score
items.summary: A digest report says Nvidia's general-purpose agent technology AVO completed all 183 levels across 25 environments on ARC-AGI-3 with a perfect score. If accurate, that would be a notable benchmark result for agentic reasoning systems.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: GTA 6 leak saga escalates as Take-Two seeks account records
items.summary: Multiple reports say Take-Two is pursuing subpoenas and account information from Microsoft, Discord, X, and Google as part of its effort to identify the source of GTA 6 leaks. The leak story has also been muddied by later fact-checking that described at least one widely circulated threat as fabricated.

items.title: Cyberleek claims around GTA 6 leak prove volatile and increasingly disputed
items.summary: Coverage this week describes a new wave of GTA 6 gameplay clips attributed to Cyberleek, alongside claims of a larger planned reveal. Other reporting says parts of the story were later exposed as fake or misleading, making the situation highly uncertain.

items.title: Microsoft details 28 Xbox releases arriving this week
items.summary: Microsoft reportedly listed 28 games coming to Xbox between August 25 and 28, with some titles also joining Game Pass immediately. The lineup includes Blood Dungeon, Once Human, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2, Metal Gear Solid: Master Collection Vol. 2, and more.

items.title: Riot’s 2XKO reportedly canceled
items.summary: Gaming coverage this morning says Riot Games has ended active development on 2XKO, the League of Legends fighting game, with remaining work expected to wrap in December. The report is being echoed across gaming news and social chatter, but it is not yet widely confirmed by an official Riot statement in the results provided.

items.title: Control Resonant physical release delayed, digital launch unchanged
items.summary: Remedy Entertainment reportedly pushed the physical edition of Control Resonant to October 15 while keeping the digital release set for September 24. The change affects only the boxed version.

items.title: Fallout series new PS5 release date announced
items.summary: One roundup states that a new Fallout series title has been confirmed for PlayStation 5 with a September 15 release date. The available result does not provide enough detail to verify which specific Fallout game this refers to.

items.title: PS5 boycott over digital-only concerns continues
items.summary: A consumer group called Does It Play? is reportedly continuing an indefinite boycott of PlayStation over Sony's plan to cancel physical disc support. The campaign is presented as ongoing pressure rather than a settled dispute.

items.title: The Duskbloods network test hit by server problems
items.summary: Japanese gaming coverage says the first day of The Duskbloods network test was canceled because server issues could not be resolved in time. The test's timing will reportedly be announced again later.
